issues.legal_issue: A High Court may decide a second appeal from an appellate decree only after formulating a substantial question of law and hearing the appeal on the formulated question, subject to the statutory proviso.
material_facts: The trial court decreed a suit seeking declarations concerning title to land, and the first appellate court reversed that decree.
The High Court restored the trial court’s decree in a second appeal.
The High Court’s judgment did not show that it had formulated a substantial question of law or heard the second appeal on a formulated question.
issues.conclusion: The High Court’s judgment could not be maintained. It was set aside and the matter was remitted to the High Court for disposal in accordance with law.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 100(3)–(5) of the Code of Civil Procedure, the memorandum of second appeal must precisely state the substantial question of law; the High Court must formulate such a question when satisfied that one is involved; and the appeal must be heard on the formulated question. The proviso permits hearing on another substantial question of law, for reasons recorded, if the case involves it. Ishwar Dass Jain v. Sohan Lal, [2000] 1 SCC 434, holds that after the 1976 amendment a High Court cannot reverse the first appellate court’s judgment without formulating a substantial question of law. Roop Singh v. Ram Singh, [2000] 3 SCC 703, reiterates that second-appeal jurisdiction is confined to substantial questions of law and does not permit interference with pure questions of fact. The Court also notes that this position was reiterated in Kanhaiyalal v. Anupkumar, JT (2002) 10 SC 98, and refers to R. Lakshmi Narayan v. Santhi, M.S.V. Raja v. Seeni Thevar, R.V.E. Venkatachala Gounder v. Arulmigu Viswesaraswami and V.P. Temple, Md. Mohammad Ali v. Jagadish Kalita, Chadat Singh v. Bahadur Ram, Kishori Lal v. Madan Gopal, and Mathakala Krishnaiah v. V. Rajagopal.

predicates.second_appeal_from_appellate_decree: A party brought a second appeal to the High Court from a decree made by a subordinate court in appeal.
predicates.no_substantial_question_formulated: The High Court did not formulate a substantial question of law for the second appeal.
predicates.appeal_not_heard_on_formulated_question: The High Court did not hear the second appeal on a substantial question of law that it had formulated.

issues.definition: When a High Court decides a second appeal from an appellate decree without formulating a substantial question of law or without hearing the appeal on a formulated question, its judgment is set aside and the matter is sent back for lawful disposal.
